Al 2025, el Estado mexicano implementa políticas, estrategias y programas para transitar hacia una economía verde que promueva la mitigación al CC y el reforzamiento del marco institucional, considerando la eficiencia energética, la promoción de energías limpias y renovables, así como producción, consumo, transporte, ciudades y agricultura sostenibles; con enfoque en salud e integrado.
planEntityVersion.description:
Texto completo del efecto directo 6: Al 2025, el Estado mexicano implementa políticas, estrategias y programas que permitan transitar hacia una economía verde que promueva la mitigación al cambio climático y el reforzamiento del marco institucional, considerando la eficiencia energética, la promoción de energías limpias y renovables, así como producción, consumo, transporte, ciudades y agricultura sostenibles; con enfoque en salud, derechos humanos, género, interculturalidad, ciclo de vida y territorio.

El Estado mexicano enfrenta múltiples retos ambientales relacionados con la creciente pérdida de ecosistemas en gran parte del territorio nacional, el deterioro de la calidad del aire en las zonas metropolitanas, la degradación edáfica y una creciente presión sobre los recursos hídricos. El crecimiento económico ha ido a la par del incremento en las emisiones de gases de efecto invernadero (GEI), el mal uso de sus recursos naturales, la generación abundante de residuos sólidos y la descarga de aguas residuales, a la vez que la cubierta remanente de bosques y selvas se reduce notablemente. Este escenario se conjuga con una disminución progresiva del gasto e implementación de políticas públicas eficaces en protección ambiental, de tal suerte que al país le cuesta más la degradación ambiental que lo que invierte para proteger el medio ambiente.

Por otra parte, el acelerado proceso de urbanización ha puesto fuertes presiones sobre los ecosistemas, tanto en el uso de los recursos naturales como por la generación de contaminantes y residuos que se vierten, con altos costos en la salud y bienestar de las personas. La gestión ineficiente y el uso insostenible de los recursos naturales afecta los modos de vida de todas las personas, pero algunos grupos poblacionales específicos, tales como los pueblos y las comunidades indígenas y rurales, con énfasis en las mujeres, quienes enfrentan barreras en el acceso y uso de recursos, son los más vulnerables ante los efectos de esas actividades irracionales.

Si bien el Estado mexicano ha fortalecido considerablemente su marco jurídico al integrar normas con reconocimiento internacional, persiste el reto de reforzar el marco institucional a nivel estatal y municipal e implementar las políticas medioambientales de manera integral y coherente, a fin de que lograr las metas del Acuerdo de París y las establecidas en la Agenda 2030 y los ODS.

planEntityVersion.description:
Pour impulser les changements escomptés sous cet effet, le système des Nations Unies entend agir sur la qualité de l’éducation congolaise à travers le renforcement de la performance de ses services, l’amélioration de l’environnement scolaire en mettant un accent particulier sur le harcèlement et d’autres facteurs de régression. Le changement ne sera pas maximal si l’action n’est pas portée sur la qualité de l’éducation congolaise avec une orientation plus accrue vers la qualité de la formation professionnelle et technique en adéquation avec les choix stratégiques du PND et qui permettra d’accélérer la diversification de l’économie à travers un meilleur capital humain. Ces actions seront portées en priorité dans les zones rurales pour bénéficier au maximum aux populations les plus pauvres et aux peuples autochtones.

Caribbean countries manage natural resources and ecosystems to strengthen their resilience and enhance the resilience and prosperity of the people and communities that depend on them.
planEntityVersion.description: Caribbean economies are highly dependent on the region’s natural resources and biodiverse ecosystems, both of which provide key services and co-benefits to people and communities. Economic resilience is, however, a critical challenge for the region in the face of environmental, climate and disaster risks, which collectively destroy natural resources and limit the region’s transformative capacity. The challenges of desertification, forest management, biodiversity loss and climate change are interrelated and need to be collectively addressed to achieve sustainable development in the Caribbean.  Both marine and terrestrial biodiversity conservation are acute issues requiring prioritization to ensure the sustainable use of ecosystems. Nature-based solutions that tackle overexploitation and address pollution and waste management should be optimised with specific attention provided to food and water security, a challenge that was further evidenced during the COVID-19 crisis.

Involving  the private sector  early on in the transformation process is  essential given its  increasingly important role in achieving inclusive sustainable development, including through public-private partnership. Involving the private sector  early on in the transformation process is  essential given its  increasingly important role in achieving inclusive sustainable development, including through public-private partnership.  An important element to this area is the establishment of innovative and sustainable financial architecture that can enable MSME access to financial markets. planEntityVersion.description:
La valorisation du capital humain impose une maitrise des questions de santé. En outre le dividende démographique n’est possible que si la population congolaise jeune active est apte sur le plan sanitaire à offrir une main d’œuvre capable d’impulser la croissance économique. Le Système des Nations Unies a un avantage comparatif considérable dans ce secteur qui compte le plus grand nombre d’agences. 

Pour apporter les changements nécessaires, le Système des Nations Unies entend agir sur les capacités techniques et opérationnelles des structures du gouvernement. Ce développement des capacités pourra ainsi permettre aux structures sanitaires d’offrir des paquets de soins complets et des services essentiels et dans la gestion des épidémies. Il faut ajouter qu’en amont, les Nations Unies agiront sur les questions d’hygiène, d’assainissement et d’eau pour réduire de façon considérable la morbidité. 

Dans une telle perspective, les actions reposeront sur l’hypothèse d’une meilleure organisation des services du Ministère de la santé et des différentes entités relevant du secteur de la santé pour faciliter le travail du système des Nations Unies.

Effet 1 : D’ici 2026, les populations bénéficient d’un système de gouvernance amélioré sur le plan institutionnel, démocratique, des droits humains, administratif et économique pour un développement inclusif et participatif, la consolidation de la paix et de l’effort humanitaire.
planEntityVersion.description:
A travers cet effet, le Système des Nations Unies entend apporter les changements aux faiblesses relevées dans la gouvernance institutionnelle, démocratiques, des droits humains de manière à favoriser les conditions de dialogue permanent entre les acteurs congolais et de renforcer la consolidation de la paix. Les institutions mises en place dans le cadre de la constitution du 25 octobre 2015 sont encore nouvelles et nécessitent de ce fait un accompagnement des partenaires au développement pour leur permettre de jouer pleinement leur rôle dans l’arène politique et sociale du pays. Un appui sera également apporté dans le renforcement des cadres stratégiques et juridiques assortis des mesures opérationnelles en rapport avec le respect des droits humains. A cet effet, les recommandations faites par ces mécanismes conventionnels des droits de l’homme et ceux de l’examen périodique universel devront contribuer de manière substantielle à l’édification de l’Etat de droit et par conséquent a la bonne gouvernance politique, administrative et économique. Il faut ainsi agir sur le développement des capacités étatiques et les acteurs non-étatiques pour appliquer les normes de gouvernance institutionnelle, administrative économique, juridique et judiciaire y compris en matière des droits de l’homme. Il faut mobiliser la société en appui à l’effort des Nations Unies et du gouvernement.

ED2. Al 2025, la población, en especial la que está en condiciones de mayor vulnerabilidad, ejerce plenamente sus derechos a la salud, educación, cultura, vivienda, alimentación, protección social y de cuidados, y accede a servicios universales y a un sistema integral de cuidados de calidad.
planEntityVersion.description: El ejercicio efectivo de los derechos sociales incluye el acceso, la disponibilidad y la calidad de los servicios, de tal suerte que se garantice su cumplimiento. En los Estados Unidos Mexicanos, el número y porcentaje de personas que tienen carencias en acceso a los servicios de salud, educación, alimentación y vivienda es muy alto, pero es el acceso a la seguridad social el derecho más rezagado. La diversidad geográfica, cultural y socioeconómica del país plantea un desafío para garantizar el ejercicio del derecho a la educación y la salud en un contexto de desigualdad y pobreza. De acuerdo con la medición multidimensional de la pobreza, hay grupos de población cuyo ejercicio de derechos se encuentra sistemáticamente comprometido, generando mayor rezago y exclusión, aunado a que la calidad, suficiencia y pertinencia de los servicios sigue siendo un reto. El Estado mexicano necesita fortalecer políticas y presupuestos públicos integrales, de vocación universalista  y enfocados a igualar la garantía de los derechos de las personas, principalmente de aquellos grupos, regiones y entidades que se encuentran en desventaja. La desigualdad en la responsabilidad social del trabajo doméstico y de cuidados no remunerado tiene un impacto negativo en la vida y el desarrollo de las mujeres, y profundiza y reproduce la pobreza y las desigualdades al restringir notablemente sus oportunidades de contar con ingresos propios o buscar opciones en el mercado laboral, y las relega de la protección social para la satisfacción autónoma de sus necesidades.

Caribbean countries manage natural resources and ecosystems to strengthen their resilience and enhance the resilience and prosperity of the people and communities that depend on them.
planEntityVersion.description: Caribbean economies are highly dependent on the region’s natural resources and biodiverse ecosystems, both of which provide key services and co-benefits to people and communities. Economic resilience is, however, a critical challenge for the region in the face of environmental, climate and disaster risks, which collectively destroy natural resources and limit the region’s transformative capacity. The challenges of desertification, forest management, biodiversity loss and climate change are interrelated and need to be collectively addressed to achieve sustainable development in the Caribbean.  Both marine and terrestrial biodiversity conservation are acute issues requiring prioritization to ensure the sustainable use of ecosystems. Nature-based solutions that tackle overexploitation and address pollution and waste management should be optimised with specific attention provided to food and water security, a challenge that was further evidenced during the COVID-19 crisis.

Outcome 4.1 - Al 2022, la institucionalidad estatal a nivel nacional, regional y local se fortalece, para la mitigación y la adaptación al cambio climático, el manejo sostenible y preservación de los recursos naturales, ecosistemas y su biodiversidad, así como la gestión de riesgos y conflictos socioambientales.
planEntityVersion.description:
En el marco de la COP 25 bajo la presidencia de Chile, el país asumió el compromiso de profundizar en la agenda de género y la acción climática.  Para ello firmó acuerdo de colaboración con el Gran Ducado de Luxemburgo para implementar el proyecto “Género y cambio climático”, implementado por l Sistema de las Naciones Unidas y el Ministerio de Medio Ambiente.  En este proyecto, participaron el Programa de las Naciones Unidas para el Desarrollo (PNUD) y la Organización de las Naciones Unidas para la Alimentación y la Agricultura (FAO) y ONU Mujeres que lideró la ejecución del proyecto. El Éxito del proyecto, implicó que, en base a los resultados y lecciones aprendidas de esta iniciativa, que el Gran Ducado de Luxemburgo, decidiera apoyar por 4 años, a partir de 2023, una iniciativa regional, liderada por la Oficina Regional de ONU Mujeres, sobre cambio climático y enfoque de género. Los antecedentes y resultados del proyecto son los siguientes:

El objetivo principal del proyecto fue generar información que permita incorporar el enfoque de género en las políticas, programas y planes nacionales sectoriales de cambio climático. 

Para lograr el objetivo, se propuso generar información estadística e indicadores que den cuenta de las brechas de género existentes y permitan contar con datos desagregados para una mejor, eficiente y justa toma de decisiones, priorizando las áreas más urgente para reducir las desigualdades y el impacto medioambiental. Se crearon indicadores y un plan de monitoreo insertos en los planes nacionales de Adaptación y Mitigación, junto con programas específicos de género que considerearon el factor climático. Finalmente, la información obtenida fue puesta a disposición pública a través de la plataforma ARClim , visibilizando la distribución de las desigualdades por género, edad y territorio de la población desde el punto de vista climático.

En segundo lugar, al considerar la poca evidencia sobre la efectividad de programas existentes   en torno a género y cambio climático, el proyecto hizo hincapié en la importancia de incluir la perspectiva de género en las políticas sobre esta materia, dando a conocer y compartiendo avances sobre aquellas implementadas en el resto del mundo. 

En tercer lugar, el proyecto también propuso fortalecer las capacidades para una transversalización de género en temáticas ambientales, de funcionarios y funcionarias del Ministerio de Medio Ambiente, sociedad civil, academia y quienes toman decisiones a nivel nacional y regional. Ello, a través de capacitaciones, charlas y cursos especializados en Género y Medio Ambiente, con el fin de generar habilidades y conocimientos valiosos que ayuden a impulsar la inclusión de una perspectiva de género en las decisiones, programas y políticas medioambientales, así como también en el diálogo ciudadano. 

En relación a los avances, a nivel nacional se integró el enfoque de género en su Contribución Determinada a nivel Nacional (CDN), se presentó la Estrategia Climática de Largo Plazo (ECLP) con metas asociadas a la equidad e igualdad de género;  con el fin de generar conocimiento frente a los efectos diferenciados del cambio climático, se conformó una Mesa de Género y Cambio Climático de carácter intersectorial y se elaboraron cinco instrumentos además de integrar y complementar estas nuevas herramientas con otras iniciativas desarrolladas por el Ministerio de Medio Ambiente de Chile, en el país y la Región, como el Manual de Gestión para la Integración del enfoque de género en la acción climática, la Lista de Chequeo para integrar género en los instrumentos de cambio climático; y el estudio Generación de indicadores y análisis sectorial sobre género y cambio climático en cuatro sectores vulnerables al cambio climático: ciudades, pesca y acuicultura, biodiversidad y agricultura, modelo innovador y que servirá de base para apoyar a los distintos sectores que en el plazo de 2 años deben elaborar un plan de acción con enfoque de género en respuesta la reciente Ley Marco de Cambio climático.

•	Diseño de guidas de buenas prácticas de refrigeración en cámaras de frio y normas mínimas de eficiencia energética (MEPS) en vitrinas  
•	Implementar 4 proyectos de demonstración en línea con las guías de buenas prácticas y las MEPS desarrolladas

Se crearon indicadores y un plan de monitoreo insertos en los planes nacionales de Adaptación y Mitigación, junto con programas específicos de género que considerearon el factor climático. Finalmente, la información obtenida fue puesta a disposición pública a través de la plataforma ARClim , visibilizando la distribución de las desigualdades por género, edad y territorio de la población desde el punto de vista climático.

En segundo lugar, al considerar la poca evidencia sobre la efectividad de programas existentes   en torno a género y cambio climático, el proyecto hizo hincapié en la importancia de incluir la perspectiva de género en las políticas sobre esta materia, dando a conocer y compartiendo avances sobre aquellas implementadas en el resto del mundo. 

En tercer lugar, el proyecto también propuso fortalecer las capacidades para una transversalización de género en temáticas ambientales, de funcionarios y funcionarias del Ministerio de Medio Ambiente, sociedad civil, academia y quienes toman decisiones a nivel nacional y regional. Ello, a través de capacitaciones, charlas y cursos especializados en Género y Medio Ambiente, con el fin de generar habilidades y conocimientos valiosos que ayuden a impulsar la inclusión de una perspectiva de género en las decisiones, programas y políticas medioambientales, así como también en el diálogo ciudadano. 

En relación a los avances, a nivel nacional se integró el enfoque de género en su Contribución Determinada a nivel Nacional (CDN), se presentó la Estrategia Climática de Largo Plazo (ECLP) con metas asociadas a la equidad e igualdad de género;  con el fin de generar conocimiento frente a los efectos diferenciados del cambio climático, se conformó una Mesa de Género y Cambio Climático de carácter intersectorial y se elaboraron cinco instrumentos además de integrar y complementar estas nuevas herramientas con otras iniciativas desarrolladas por el Ministerio de Medio Ambiente de Chile, en el país y la Región, como el Manual de Gestión para la Integración del enfoque de género en la acción climática, la Lista de Chequeo para integrar género en los instrumentos de cambio climático; y el estudio Generación de indicadores y análisis sectorial sobre género y cambio climático en cuatro sectores vulnerables al cambio climático: ciudades, pesca y acuicultura, biodiversidad y agricultura, modelo innovador y que servirá de base para apoyar a los distintos sectores que en el plazo de 2 años deben elaborar un plan de acción con enfoque de género en respuesta la reciente Ley Marco de Cambio climático.

La Fase III del plan de gestión de eliminación de HCFC contiene cuatro líneas estratégicas, dentro de las cuales se encuentran la Línea Estratégica #2: “Programa de apoyo al sector de refrigeración y aire acondicionado” y la Línea Estratégica #4 “Programa de Monitoreo”, que incluyen las siguientes actividades:

1. Capacitación en mejores prácticas de refrigeración y aire acondicionado, y certificación de mujeres técnicas en habilidades RAC, para mejorar la gestión de HCFC y sus alternativas, reduciendo las emisiones al medio ambiente.
2. Asistencia técnica al sector RAC, a través del Programa Cero Fugas, para la realización de proyectos piloto en sistemas frigoríficos revisando y controlando sus fugas, consumo energético, consumos de refrigerante, para mejorar sus parámetros de rendimiento.
3. Asistencia técnica para los centros de recuperación, para mejorar su operación y capacidades de control de calidad para refrigerantes regenerados: y
4. Supervisión de la ejecución de las actividades del plan de gestión de eliminación de HCFC-III.

1) Programa Tu Oportunidad: During 2022, SCE Chile launched a new evidence-based methodology (based on the results of a previously developed pilot program), with two learning routes, one towards entrepreneurship and the other towards employability, depending to the participant’s profile (beginner/advanced). This methodology was implemented by the AIEP, a renown technical education institute, that undertook the mission to address the economic empowerment of women, migrants, and indigenous people with socioeconomic vulnerability through a sustainable model for technical education in this area. In addition, this institution is leveraging its vast network of private and public actors to increase opportunities for participants through referrals to entrepreneurship and employment clusters. As part of its sustainability program its community of students and graduates are encouraged to engage in volunteering activities.  There are currently 6,476 women participating in this program and 1,660 have been mentored by the 140 volunteer mentors who belong to the Your Opportunity Mentor Network. Another 542 women have been trained to become mentors to other SCE women as well as agents of change in their communities.  In terms of impact, and according to the follow-up survey of graduates three and six months after graduating, 37% of women improved their income; 16% of women found employment; 20% returned to formal education; 24% started a new business; 36% improved the business they already had; and 44% continued their education, all thanks to the AIEP program.
The AIEP program also strengthened its regional and national partnerships, identifying opportunities for collaborative projects and establishing labor reference protocols with the Ministry of the Interior, local governments and civil society organizations. Specifically in the northern region of the country, partnerships for the implementation of programmes and linkages have been strengthened (including SERNAMEG - National Women's Service, and SECREDUC - Regional Education Agency). More importantly, SCE Chile has been actively involved in the IOM/UNHCR-led roundtable on migration. In the southern zone, alliances have been developed in the Magallanes Region (including SERNAMEG, INDAP - National Institute of Agricultural Development, Venezuelans in Patagonia and other civil society institutions) to include more women from the most remote areas of the country. Simultaneously, SCE Chile has advanced in developing new partnerships with institutions and agencies for this new period of implementation (Ministry of Social Development,  INJUV, University of La Frontera and civil society).
In addition, SCE Chile led the public-private roundtable "More women in STEM education" which was developed jointly with Fundación País Digital (funded and supported by TELCOs and Technology companies in Chile) facilitating discussion among civil society actors, companies, universities and government to provide critical inputs and a gender approach for public policies in STEM education. Finally, SCE Chile prepared and disseminated a policy  report on Second Chance Education with a Gender Perspective with good practices and recommendations, contributing to public policy on online education and training for adult women.
2) Programa Originarias: During 2022, UN Women through its Originarias Programme contributed to the economic and social empowerment of more than 1,000 indigenous women in Chile, contributing towards the achievement of Sustainable Development Goals 1, 4, 5, 8, 12 and 17 of the 2030 Agenda and the strategic priorities of economic integration, education for work, citizen participation and effective exercise of human rights of the United Nations Cooperation Framework for Sustainable Development in Chile 2019-2022. 
Training and technical assistance provided by UN Women in conjunction with indigenous facilitators and academic and state institutions enabled more than 1,000 indigenous women to strengthen their leadership and advocacy skills, and more than 400 indigenous women entrepreneurs to access services, goods and resources, improving their opportunities for economic integration and participation in decision-making. 
The strategy implemented to actively train and promote the participation of indigenous trainers in intercultural learning spaces was a key factor for the success of the Originarias Program. The facilitators of the Originarias Program are mostly indigenous women (95%) who were trained in UN Women Training of Trainers schools. During 2012, these women, through the Originarias Program, participated in learning opportunities aimed at non-indigenous youth and adults and contributed to facilitate dialogues between indigenous women to elaborate proposals for economic development agendas. Finally, within the framework of the exercise of cultural rights, the program developed a school to improve the Aymara language skills of 28 intercultural educators, benefitting indirectly more than 4,000 indigenous children in the Tarapacá region.
As a result of the impacts generated by the Originarias Program, during 2022 a new donation agreement was signed with Teck Resources Ltd. for a total of 5.25 million dollars, which will enable the implementation of a 5-year process that will escalate over the years to incorporate new management strategies and financing mechanisms, to increasing the benefits  resulting from the Original Program and make these sustainable in the long term, placing the responsibility of strategic development on indigenous women themselves. With a proven methodology for empowerment, based on the integration of a rights, gender perspective and interculturality approach, the Originarias Program has the potential to be replicated in other territories, within Chile and in Latin America.
3) Proyecto Recuperación económica MPTF: Under the framework of the successful implementation of the MPTF program, UN Women during 2022 reached and established strategic alliances with many sectors of society (public, private, civil society, and communities), facilitating the  progress in different areas of gender equality, providing tools to improve women's economic opportunities, promoting leadership of micro-entrepreneur women, working with their businesses to include a gender perspective in their operation, raising awareness in the population in care co-responsibility issues, and generating information to guide the design of local and global policies.
One significant outcome of the program is related to the partnerships and collaboration networks that were created during its implementation and are still in place after the project's conclusion. The coordination of networks with different sectors and actors, the private and public sectors, employers and workers organizations, civil society, communities, and other initiatives from the UN, were crucial for creating better economic opportunities for women from the sectors most affected by the pandemic (heads of the household, migrants, women from rural areas, and caregivers). The MujeresEmplea.org virtual platform consolidated the offer of work and training opportunities, access to funds, and subsidies to entrepreneurship and care services (with more than 100 updated publications), with more than 67,000 visits during the implementation period. In parallel, the Activa Empresarias platform was created to connect the demand of products and services of large companies with the supply of companies led by women. 
A pilot training, mentoring, and community care services program was successfully designed and implemented. It positively impacted the insertion of women into the labor market. It allowed their economic activation mainly in three communes of Chile with high female social vulnerability rates (Renca, Padre las Casas, and San Pedro de Atacama). More than 9,000 women were trained in digital skills for employment and/or entrepreneurship, and more than 350 women were mentored for their labor insertion. The job fairs for women offered more than 33,000 job openings, to which more than 3,000 women applied. 
The childcare service was available in the selected territories to facilitate the access of their caregivers to training and work opportunities, providing care to 125 children per day.
A network of 300 women was trained and certified in care services, laying the foundations to establish a national caregiver's network, which the Government of Chile is currently promoting.
Awareness-raising and promoting care co-responsibility had a great reach among companies in the selected territories and the general population, promoting gender equality through communication plans and workshops designed for each target audience.

En relación a los avances, a nivel nacional se integró el enfoque de género en su Contribución Determinada a nivel Nacional (CDN), se presentó la Estrategia Climática de Largo Plazo (ECLP) con metas asociadas a la equidad e igualdad de género;  con el fin de generar conocimiento frente a los efectos diferenciados del cambio climático, se conformó una Mesa de Género y Cambio Climático de carácter intersectorial y se elaboraron cinco instrumentos además de integrar y complementar estas nuevas herramientas con otras iniciativas desarrolladas por el Ministerio de Medio Ambiente de Chile, en el país y la Región, como el Manual de Gestión para la Integración del enfoque de género en la acción climática, la Lista de Chequeo para integrar género en los instrumentos de cambio climático; y el estudio Generación de indicadores y análisis sectorial sobre género y cambio climático en cuatro sectores vulnerables al cambio climático: ciudades, pesca y acuicultura, biodiversidad y agricultura, modelo innovador y que servirá de base para apoyar a los distintos sectores que en el plazo de 2 años deben elaborar un plan de acción con enfoque de género en respuesta la reciente Ley Marco de Cambio climático.
Elaboración de indicadores de género, Fortalecimiento institucional y  acciones de difusión

planEntityVersion.description:
1) Programa Tu Oportunidad: During 2022, SCE Chile launched a new evidence-based methodology (based on the results of a previously developed pilot program), with two learning routes, one towards entrepreneurship and the other towards employability, depending to the participant’s profile (beginner/advanced). This methodology was implemented by the AIEP, a renown technical education institute, that undertook the mission to address the economic empowerment of women, migrants, and indigenous people with socioeconomic vulnerability through a sustainable model for technical education in this area. In addition, this institution is leveraging its vast network of private and public actors to increase opportunities for participants through referrals to entrepreneurship and employment clusters. As part of its sustainability program its community of students and graduates are encouraged to engage in volunteering activities.  There are currently 6,476 women participating in this program and 1,660 have been mentored by the 140 volunteer mentors who belong to the Your Opportunity Mentor Network. Another 542 women have been trained to become mentors to other SCE women as well as agents of change in their communities.  In terms of impact, and according to the follow-up survey of graduates three and six months after graduating, 37% of women improved their income; 16% of women found employment; 20% returned to formal education; 24% started a new business; 36% improved the business they already had; and 44% continued their education, all thanks to the AIEP program.
The AIEP program also strengthened its regional and national partnerships, identifying opportunities for collaborative projects and establishing labor reference protocols with the Ministry of the Interior, local governments and civil society organizations. Specifically in the northern region of the country, partnerships for the implementation of programmes and linkages have been strengthened (including SERNAMEG - National Women's Service, and SECREDUC - Regional Education Agency). More importantly, SCE Chile has been actively involved in the IOM/UNHCR-led roundtable on migration. In the southern zone, alliances have been developed in the Magallanes Region (including SERNAMEG, INDAP - National Institute of Agricultural Development, Venezuelans in Patagonia and other civil society institutions) to include more women from the most remote areas of the country. Simultaneously, SCE Chile has advanced in developing new partnerships with institutions and agencies for this new period of implementation (Ministry of Social Development,  INJUV, University of La Frontera and civil society).
In addition, SCE Chile led the public-private roundtable "More women in STEM education" which was developed jointly with Fundación País Digital (funded and supported by TELCOs and Technology companies in Chile) facilitating discussion among civil society actors, companies, universities and government to provide critical inputs and a gender approach for public policies in STEM education. Finally, SCE Chile prepared and disseminated a policy  report on Second Chance Education with a Gender Perspective with good practices and recommendations, contributing to public policy on online education and training for adult women.
2) Programa Originarias: During 2022, UN Women through its Originarias Programme contributed to the economic and social empowerment of more than 1,000 indigenous women in Chile, contributing towards the achievement of Sustainable Development Goals 1, 4, 5, 8, 12 and 17 of the 2030 Agenda and the strategic priorities of economic integration, education for work, citizen participation and effective exercise of human rights of the United Nations Cooperation Framework for Sustainable Development in Chile 2019-2022. 
Training and technical assistance provided by UN Women in conjunction with indigenous facilitators and academic and state institutions enabled more than 1,000 indigenous women to strengthen their leadership and advocacy skills, and more than 400 indigenous women entrepreneurs to access services, goods and resources, improving their opportunities for economic integration and participation in decision-making. 
The strategy implemented to actively train and promote the participation of indigenous trainers in intercultural learning spaces was a key factor for the success of the Originarias Program. The facilitators of the Originarias Program are mostly indigenous women (95%) who were trained in UN Women Training of Trainers schools. During 2012, these women, through the Originarias Program, participated in learning opportunities aimed at non-indigenous youth and adults and contributed to facilitate dialogues between indigenous women to elaborate proposals for economic development agendas. Finally, within the framework of the exercise of cultural rights, the program developed a school to improve the Aymara language skills of 28 intercultural educators, benefitting indirectly more than 4,000 indigenous children in the Tarapacá region.
As a result of the impacts generated by the Originarias Program, during 2022 a new donation agreement was signed with Teck Resources Ltd. for a total of 5.25 million dollars, which will enable the implementation of a 5-year process that will escalate over the years to incorporate new management strategies and financing mechanisms, to increasing the benefits  resulting from the Original Program and make these sustainable in the long term, placing the responsibility of strategic development on indigenous women themselves. With a proven methodology for empowerment, based on the integration of a rights, gender perspective and interculturality approach, the Originarias Program has the potential to be replicated in other territories, within Chile and in Latin America.
3) Proyecto Recuperación económica MPTF: Under the framework of the successful implementation of the MPTF program, UN Women during 2022 reached and established strategic alliances with many sectors of society (public, private, civil society, and communities), facilitating the  progress in different areas of gender equality, providing tools to improve women's economic opportunities, promoting leadership of micro-entrepreneur women, working with their businesses to include a gender perspective in their operation, raising awareness in the population in care co-responsibility issues, and generating information to guide the design of local and global policies.
One significant outcome of the program is related to the partnerships and collaboration networks that were created during its implementation and are still in place after the project's conclusion. The coordination of networks with different sectors and actors, the private and public sectors, employers and workers organizations, civil society, communities, and other initiatives from the UN, were crucial for creating better economic opportunities for women from the sectors most affected by the pandemic (heads of the household, migrants, women from rural areas, and caregivers). The MujeresEmplea.org virtual platform consolidated the offer of work and training opportunities, access to funds, and subsidies to entrepreneurship and care services (with more than 100 updated publications), with more than 67,000 visits during the implementation period. In parallel, the Activa Empresarias platform was created to connect the demand of products and services of large companies with the supply of companies led by women. 
A pilot training, mentoring, and community care services program was successfully designed and implemented. It positively impacted the insertion of women into the labor market. It allowed their economic activation mainly in three communes of Chile with high female social vulnerability rates (Renca, Padre las Casas, and San Pedro de Atacama). More than 9,000 women were trained in digital skills for employment and/or entrepreneurship, and more than 350 women were mentored for their labor insertion. The job fairs for women offered more than 33,000 job openings, to which more than 3,000 women applied. 
The childcare service was available in the selected territories to facilitate the access of their caregivers to training and work opportunities, providing care to 125 children per day.
A network of 300 women was trained and certified in care services, laying the foundations to establish a national caregiver's network, which the Government of Chile is currently promoting.
Awareness-raising and promoting care co-responsibility had a great reach among companies in the selected territories and the general population, promoting gender equality through communication plans and workshops designed for each target audience.

Another 542 women have been trained to become mentors to other SCE women as well as agents of change in their communities.  In terms of impact, and according to the follow-up survey of graduates three and six months after graduating, 37% of women improved their income; 16% of women found employment; 20% returned to formal education; 24% started a new business; 36% improved the business they already had; and 44% continued their education, all thanks to the AIEP program.
The AIEP program also strengthened its regional and national partnerships, identifying opportunities for collaborative projects and establishing labor reference protocols with the Ministry of the Interior, local governments and civil society organizations. Specifically in the northern region of the country, partnerships for the implementation of programmes and linkages have been strengthened (including SERNAMEG - National Women's Service, and SECREDUC - Regional Education Agency). More importantly, SCE Chile has been actively involved in the IOM/UNHCR-led roundtable on migration. In the southern zone, alliances have been developed in the Magallanes Region (including SERNAMEG, INDAP - National Institute of Agricultural Development, Venezuelans in Patagonia and other civil society institutions) to include more women from the most remote areas of the country. Simultaneously, SCE Chile has advanced in developing new partnerships with institutions and agencies for this new period of implementation (Ministry of Social Development,  INJUV, University of La Frontera and civil society).
In addition, SCE Chile led the public-private roundtable "More women in STEM education" which was developed jointly with Fundación País Digital (funded and supported by TELCOs and Technology companies in Chile) facilitating discussion among civil society actors, companies, universities and government to provide critical inputs and a gender approach for public policies in STEM education. Finally, SCE Chile prepared and disseminated a policy  report on Second Chance Education with a Gender Perspective with good practices and recommendations, contributing to public policy on online education and training for adult women.
2) Programa Originarias: During 2022, UN Women through its Originarias Programme contributed to the economic and social empowerment of more than 1,000 indigenous women in Chile, contributing towards the achievement of Sustainable Development Goals 1, 4, 5, 8, 12 and 17 of the 2030 Agenda and the strategic priorities of economic integration, education for work, citizen participation and effective exercise of human rights of the United Nations Cooperation Framework for Sustainable Development in Chile 2019-2022. 
Training and technical assistance provided by UN Women in conjunction with indigenous facilitators and academic and state institutions enabled more than 1,000 indigenous women to strengthen their leadership and advocacy skills, and more than 400 indigenous women entrepreneurs to access services, goods and resources, improving their opportunities for economic integration and participation in decision-making. 
The strategy implemented to actively train and promote the participation of indigenous trainers in intercultural learning spaces was a key factor for the success of the Originarias Program. The facilitators of the Originarias Program are mostly indigenous women (95%) who were trained in UN Women Training of Trainers schools. During 2012, these women, through the Originarias Program, participated in learning opportunities aimed at non-indigenous youth and adults and contributed to facilitate dialogues between indigenous women to elaborate proposals for economic development agendas. Finally, within the framework of the exercise of cultural rights, the program developed a school to improve the Aymara language skills of 28 intercultural educators, benefitting indirectly more than 4,000 indigenous children in the Tarapacá region.
As a result of the impacts generated by the Originarias Program, during 2022 a new donation agreement was signed with Teck Resources Ltd. for a total of 5.25 million dollars, which will enable the implementation of a 5-year process that will escalate over the years to incorporate new management strategies and financing mechanisms, to increasing the benefits  resulting from the Original Program and make these sustainable in the long term, placing the responsibility of strategic development on indigenous women themselves. With a proven methodology for empowerment, based on the integration of a rights, gender perspective and interculturality approach, the Originarias Program has the potential to be replicated in other territories, within Chile and in Latin America.
3) Proyecto Recuperación económica MPTF: Under the framework of the successful implementation of the MPTF program, UN Women during 2022 reached and established strategic alliances with many sectors of society (public, private, civil society, and communities), facilitating the  progress in different areas of gender equality, providing tools to improve women's economic opportunities, promoting leadership of micro-entrepreneur women, working with their businesses to include a gender perspective in their operation, raising awareness in the population in care co-responsibility issues, and generating information to guide the design of local and global policies.
One significant outcome of the program is related to the partnerships and collaboration networks that were created during its implementation and are still in place after the project's conclusion. The coordination of networks with different sectors and actors, the private and public sectors, employers and workers organizations, civil society, communities, and other initiatives from the UN, were crucial for creating better economic opportunities for women from the sectors most affected by the pandemic (heads of the household, migrants, women from rural areas, and caregivers). The MujeresEmplea.org virtual platform consolidated the offer of work and training opportunities, access to funds, and subsidies to entrepreneurship and care services (with more than 100 updated publications), with more than 67,000 visits during the implementation period. In parallel, the Activa Empresarias platform was created to connect the demand of products and services of large companies with the supply of companies led by women. 
A pilot training, mentoring, and community care services program was successfully designed and implemented. It positively impacted the insertion of women into the labor market. It allowed their economic activation mainly in three communes of Chile with high female social vulnerability rates (Renca, Padre las Casas, and San Pedro de Atacama). More than 9,000 women were trained in digital skills for employment and/or entrepreneurship, and more than 350 women were mentored for their labor insertion. The job fairs for women offered more than 33,000 job openings, to which more than 3,000 women applied. 
The childcare service was available in the selected territories to facilitate the access of their caregivers to training and work opportunities, providing care to 125 children per day.
A network of 300 women was trained and certified in care services, laying the foundations to establish a national caregiver's network, which the Government of Chile is currently promoting.
Awareness-raising and promoting care co-responsibility had a great reach among companies in the selected territories and the general population, promoting gender equality through communication plans and workshops designed for each target audience.

planEntityVersion.description: Outcome 3.1: National and sub-national capacities and systems are strengthened and are informed by data underpinning efficient, inclusive, and gender-responsive crisis response, recovery planning and green economic growth.

•	Institutional Capacity Development: The government’s strong response to the impact of the war has demonstrated that past investments in institutions have resulted in strong systems. The UN will continue to support government institutions and ministries to further grow capacity and adapt to the new challenging context. Key sectors targeted for support and institutional capacity development include security, trade transport connectivity, justice, agriculture, science, innovations, culture, media, public administration, urban, digital transformation, human capital development, rule of law, anticorruption/integrity and responding to organised crime, the care economy, and others. Government capacity for protecting and monitoring human rights and documenting violations, reinforce social cohesion and inclusion, and implementing commitments under the Women, Peace and Security (WPS) Agenda, especially women’s meaningful role in decision making processes, and Youth, Peace and Security Agenda will also be supported.
planEntityVersion.name: Institutional capacity development
National systems are able to effectively plan for and implement inclusive recovery
planEntityVersion.description: Outcome 3.1: National and sub-national capacities and systems are strengthened and are informed by data underpinning efficient, inclusive, and gender-responsive crisis response, recovery planning and green economic growth.

•	Data Generation: In collaboration with the government and relevant ministries, the UN will assist in conducting sector assessments to inform inclusive national recovery planning and implementation. This will include the generation, analysis, and utilization of high-quality data, including gender and LNOB data. Notable assessments include RDNA 3, Voluntary National Review, the SIDAR housing damage database, the Social Cohesion and Reconciliation (SCORE) Index, the SCORE-inspired Holistic Assessment of Resilience of Population (SHARP), the Human Rights Progress Study, Country Gender Equality Profile, satellite imagery for monitoring cultural heritage damage, Condition of Return Assessment, General Population Survey, Mobility and Needs Assessment, Rapid Needs Assessment, Solid Fuel Assessment, Area Baseline for registered IDPs, Intentions and Perspectives of IDPs in Ukraine, and ad-hoc investigations related to community participation and shifting conditions, etc.
planEntityVersion.name: Data generation
Strengthening Systems
planEntityVersion.description:
Result 2.1: National capacities are strengthened and use data for efficient crisis response and recovery planning. Indicative intervention areas:
•	Data generation to inform recovery planning and implementation: In partnership with the government and relevant line ministries and authorities the UN will support sector assessments that will be used to inform national recovery planning and implementation. Examples include assessments related to human impact, war damage, gender, protection, monitoring environmental impact of war, energy systems, WASH systems, market and value chain, agri-business, forestry, nuclear installations, etc. 
•	Institutional capacity development for national partners: The government’s strong response to the impact of the war has demonstrated that past investments in institutions have resulted in strong systems. The UN will continue to support government institutions and ministries to further grow capacity and adapt and adjust to the new challenging context. Key sectors targeted for support and institutional capacity development include security, justice, agriculture, education, health, social protection, and environment sectors. The focus of capacity strengthening will be on leading crisis management, emergency response and recovery planning and implementation. Government capacity for protecting and monitoring human rights and documenting violations, and implementing commitments under the Women, Peace and Security Agenda and Youth, Peace and Security Agenda, will also be supported as will strengthening capacity of local civil society and volunteer groups to participate and engage in emergency response and early recovery. Provision of technical expertise for macro-economic forecasting and policy advocacy from an LNOB perspective will also be a focus area.

Result 2.2: Early recovery interventions are effective in increasing inclusive human development, promoting a sustainable green economy and building a resilient society. Indicative intervention areas:

•	Infrastructure Reconstruction: Mine action, debris removal, reconstruction of critical infrastructure (health centres, schools, WASH, agriculture, IT, etc), implementation of affordable housing solutions.
•	Social Protection: Support to strengthening national social protection systems, including child protection systems, and promotion of alignment of multipurpose cash assistance to existing national systems.  
•	Education: Safe, secure and inclusive learning, integrated approaches to psychosocial support, social and emotional learning, and life skills education, continuity of learning, reintegration of teachers, researchers and scientists.
•	Health: Recovery and transformation of health systems, including access to pharmaceuticals and vaccinations, cold chain systems strengthening, WASH systems, digital healthcare solutions to improve access to and the quality of maternal and child healthcare services, support to mental health services, and prosthetics for victims of war.  
•	Food Security:  Maintain critical food production systems and support agri-food supply chains, markets and exports. Expand capacity for agricultural product storage and export.
•	Livelihoods and Economic Growth: Income solutions for IDPs, war affected and most vulnerable, support to affected women and youth in livelihoods recovery, skills development, business support, entrepreneurship training, access to finance, networks, markets and culture. Mobilize the private sector in humanitarian response. Strengthen labour market governance focusing on decent work. Sustainable industrial recovery, development of competitive and resource-efficient processing industries.
•	Energy and Environment: Winterization, mitigating the energy crisis, preparedness for next heating season. Connecting buildings to energy monitoring tools and energy efficient technologies. Support to energy system repair and reconstruction. Environmental clean-up and remediation, clean transport and green reconstruction. Promote bio-energy use in agriculture, sustainable natural resource management. Sustainable and inclusive environmental governance and advocacy on environmental impact of war.

Renforcement de l’État de droit, promotion des droits humains, consolidation de la démocratie et de la paix ainsi que de la cohésion sociale
planEntityVersion.description:
Cette priorité stratégique des Nations Unies est liée au PCE à travers:
-PDI 2020-2024:Garantir la paix, la sécurité et la stabilité du pays et consolider la démocratie ; réformer et moderniser les administrations pour plus de visibilité, d’efficience, de qualité et pour une meilleure gestion des carrières ; promouvoir une justice équitable au service de l’émergence
-Catalyseur 1 du PCE : Un cadre politique et institutionnel réformé et plus stable
-Condition 3 du PCE : Cadre rénové de dialogue politique sur le développement.

planEntityVersion.name: Effet UNSDCF  4 :D’ici à 2026, les institutions publiques sont plus inclusives, efficaces, redevables et résilientes et renforcent la participation citoyenne à la vie publique, la cohésion sociale, les droits de l’homme, l’égalité de genre et la démocratie

Valorisation du dividende démographique et promotion de l’offre, de la demande et de l’utilisation inclusive et équitable de services sociaux de qualité par les populations, particulièrement les plus vulnérables
planEntityVersion.description:
Cette priorité stratégique des Nations Unies est liée au PCE à travers :
-PDI 2020-2024: Promouvoir un système de santé aux normes internationales pour un capital humain performant ; promouvoir l’accès équitable à une éducation et un enseignement propice à l’épanouissement du capital humain et à la promotion des valeurs nationales et la promotion scientifique
-Catalyseur 3 du PCE:  Un capital humain qui prépare l’avenir.

planEntityVersion.name: Effet UNSDCF  3 :D’ici 2026, la population comorienne, particulièrement les plus vulnérables, tire profit du dividende démographique et utilise davantage de services adéquats, inclusifs, équitables, sensibles au genre, pérennes et de qualité de santé, de nutrition, d’éducation, de protection sociale, de prise en charge des victimes de violences
Promotion d’une économie compétitive, moderne, résiliente et créatrice d’emplois décents grâce à une croissance forte, durable et inclusive
planEntityVersion.description:
Cette priorité stratégique des Nations Unies est liée au PCE à travers:
-PDI 2020-2024: Relancer l’économie pour une croissance de 6 % ; favoriser la croissance et améliorer les conditions et le cadre de vie des populations ; favoriser le décollage rapide de l’économie et améliorer la circulation de l’information au sein de la population pour une forte cohésion sociale ; faire des sous-secteurs des leviers du développement socio-économique.
-Catalyseur 3 du PCE:  Un capital humain qui prépare l’avenir, Socles 1/2/4 du PCE.
-Catalyseur 4 du PCE : Des réformes structurelles pour un environnement compétitif conductif

planEntityVersion.name: Effet UNSDCF  2 : D’ici 2026, la population comorienne, et notamment les plus vulnérables, jouit d’une prospérité partagée, bâtie sur une économie plus compétitive et inclusive, sur des partenariats publics-privés renouvelés, et dans une perspective de croissance durable tournée vers les secteurs d’avenir (économie verte, bleue et numérique)
Renforcement de la résilience écologique et de la gestion durable et intégrée des écosystèmes terrestres et marins ainsi que des biens et services écosystémiques

-PDI 2020-2024: La gestion durable de l’environnement à travers le renforcement de la protection des ressources naturelles et de la biodiversité, la lutte contre le changement climatique et l’amélioration de la gestion des déchets.
-Catalyseur 2 du PCE:  Des infrastructures à niveau pour une économie performante.

-PDI 2020-2024: Relancer l’économie pour une croissance de 6 % ; favoriser la croissance et améliorer les conditions et le cadre de vie des populations ; favoriser le décollage rapide de l’économie et améliorer la circulation de l’information au sein de la population pour une forte cohésion sociale ; faire des sous-secteurs des leviers du développement socio-économique.
-Catalyseur 3 du PCE:  Un capital humain qui prépare l’avenir, Socles 1/2/4 du PCE.
-Catalyseur 4 du PCE : Des réformes structurelles pour un environnement compétitif conductif

More productive and competitive business ecosystem designed to improve people's standards of living and well-being
planEntityVersion.description: Outcome 1: The small size of Caribbean economies and the shortfalls in innovation and digital transformation influence the level of productivity and overall competitiveness of the region. Achieving sustainable transformation of the Caribbean business environment requires the enhanced productivity of micro, small and medium-sized enterprises’ (MSMEs), which can only be achieved by creating a more productive and competitive business ecosystem. Involving  the private sector  early on in the transformation process is  essential given its  increasingly important role in achieving inclusive sustainable development, including through public-private partnership. Involving the private sector  early on in the transformation process is  essential given its  increasingly important role in achieving inclusive sustainable development, including through public-private partnership.  An important element to this area is the establishment of innovative and sustainable financial architecture that can enable MSME access to financial markets. The United Nations can play an important interlocuter role between private-sector financiers, the public sector and other (international) financial institutions.

By 2027 people in the United Republic of Tanzania, especially the most vulnerable, participate in and benefit from government institutions and systems that promote peace and justice, are gender responsive, inclusive, accountable and representative, and are compliant with international human rights norms and standards.
planEntityVersion.description: The enabling environment outcome is aligned to the interventions for human development in the FYDP III, where the focus is on good governance and rule of law, effective and efficient justice service delivery system, peace security and political stability. It contributes to the governance and resilience pillar of the ZADEP. Under this outcome the UN will work to support the renewal of the social contract and to support the closing of the gap between the people and the institutions that serve them as outlined in the Secretary General’s report on “Our Common Agenda.” Towards this, the UN will work on ensuring that “By 2027 the most vulnerable, participate in and benefit from government institutions and systems that promote peace and justice, are gender responsive, inclusive, accountable and representative, and are compliant with international human rights norms and standards”.

During the reporting period, in March 2022 the mainland Government reviewed and updated the national social protection policy and implementing strategy. The Government conducted five consultations with  different stakeholders from social assistance; social security; productive inclusion and social insurances.  Currently a cabinet paper has been drafted to be submitted to the cabinet. 
The mid-term review of the  productive social safety net program was successfully carried out in January 2022. PSSN II has expanded coverage from 70 percent to 100 percent to all villages and Shehia in mainland and Zanzibar with an estimated 5,180,684  beneficiaries of which 55.7 percent were females and 44.3 percent were males. The total number of households is 1,375,107.  PSSN II impact evaluation design was completed, and the survey questionnaire developed. A total of 434 villages from 32 PAAs were sampled for the evaluation. Training of enumerators on questionnaire management was done and completed and enumerators deployed to conduct data collection in sampled areas.  Total of 60,779 beneficiaries out of 97,430 were found with high level of disability and confirmed as being eligible for disability benefit and  45,875 disability beneficiaries were paid during the  July/August payment period in 2022.

By 2027 People in the United Republic of Tanzania working in MSMEs and small-scale agriculture, especially the most vulnerable, achieve increased, more sustainable productivity and incomes with more equitable access to productive resources.
planEntityVersion.description: The prosperity outcome contributes to the national FYDP III economic growth and infrastructure pillars, as well as the economic transformation pillar of ZADEP. The outcome is specifically aligned to the interventions for deepening industrialisation and service provision, together with investment and trade promotion in the FYDP III, particularly those related to agriculture, manufacturing, science technology and innovation, and the blue economy. The CCA shows that economic growth is primarily benefitting wealthier urban households. As a result of the UN system’s commitment to ensuring that no one is left behind, a key focus of this outcome is on ensuring that the majority of Tanzanians who are engaged and depend on smallholder agriculture and in MSMEs for their livelihoods – also benefit through increased incomes and productivity. These two activities contribute significantly to Tanzania’s objective to achieve upper middle-income economy status

People in the Caribbean and communities actively contribute to and benefit from building and maintaining safer, fairer, more inclusive, and equitable societies
planEntityVersion.description: The Caribbean struggles with high rates of crime, inequality and inequity that adversely impacts the lives and realities of people living the Caribbean. Personal safety and security are threatened both by violence in the home and in the community and impacts the ability of people to live full and productive lives. It is crucial to tackle the root causes that hinder the creation of safe, fair, inclusive, and equitable societies and which promote and perpetuate violence and insecurity.

Regional and national laws, policies, systems, and institutions improve access to justice and promote peace, social cohesion, and security
planEntityVersion.description: Citizen security and social cohesion in the Caribbean region is threatened by high levels of crime and violence, including gender-based violence, fueled by social inequalities that interact with illicit external flows, like the trafficking in drugs and weapons, and by corruption.  To ensure that societies are safe, fair, and cohesive, it is necessary that an enabling environment is created, and duty bearers are mobilized to effect change.

planEntityVersion.name: SUR- 7.1 Programmes and policies developed to improve institutions and access to justice and security
Caribbean countries manage natural resources and ecosystems to strengthen their resilience and enhance the resilience and prosperity of the people and communities that depend on them.
planEntityVersion.description: Caribbean economies are highly dependent on the region’s natural resources and biodiverse ecosystems, both of which provide key services and co-benefits to people and communities. Economic resilience is, however, a critical challenge for the region in the face of environmental, climate and disaster risks, which collectively destroy natural resources and limit the region’s transformative capacity. The challenges of desertification, forest management, biodiversity loss and climate change are interrelated and need to be collectively addressed to achieve sustainable development in the Caribbean.  Both marine and terrestrial biodiversity conservation are acute issues requiring prioritization to ensure the sustainable use of ecosystems. Nature-based solutions that tackle overexploitation and address pollution and waste management should be optimised with specific attention provided to food and water security, a challenge that was further evidenced during the COVID-19 crisis.

planEntityVersion.name: SUR- 6.1 [Natural Resource Management] Institutions strengthened to improve natural resource management for food and water security

planEntityVersion.description:
La visión del subgrupo es ayudar al Estado Plurinacional de Bolivia a acelerar su transformación hacia una industrialización inclusiva y sostenible con oportunidades de empleo digno y trabajo decente hacia la recuperación socioeconómica, aprovechando las oportunidades de desarrollo industrial sostenible para lograr la Agenda 2030 y los ODS. Más que nunca, dado que la primera prioridad definida por el Gobierno es la reactivación económica, abrir caminos inclusivos y sostenibles con trabajo decente hacia el desarrollo industrial requiere enfoques sistémicos e integrales. El impacto de la industria se produce en sistemas cada vez más complejos, influenciados por las tendencias globales, la gobernanza multinivel y los avances tecnológicos exponenciales, con una gran variedad de partes interesadas involucradas en horizontes a más largo plazo. Asimismo, ese desarrollo industrial debe apuntar a cumplir con la Agenda 2030, favoreciendo el principio de "No Dejar a Nadie Atrás". En este sentido, se requiere enfocar las acciones en promoción de oportunidades de empleos formales y las condiciones de trabajo decente, en cumplimiento de la normativa laboral internacional y nacional vigentes. Al mismo tiempo, se debe trabajar en prevee reforzar las intervenciones para mejorar el acceso a mercados con productos / servicios de valor agregado.  

Para asegurar que la industrialización beneficie a todas y todos, permitiendo el acceso a los insumos y productos de fabricación y los dividendos industriales, se requiere que los esfuerzos sean concertados entre los actores públicos, privados y la sociedad civil, para garantizar  el desarrollo industrial sea sostenible, inclusivo y justo, con el fin de que las empresas puedan desarrollarse y que las personas puedan acceder a los nuevos empleos, con habilidades actualizadas, en condiciones de trabajo decente y alineadas a los requerimientos de los mercados laborales; en este marco, es importante señalar que los resultados y programas se deben constituir, también, en la agenda pública.

-El desarrollo industrial inclusivo y sostenible con trabajo decente, es considerado una estratégia esencial hacia una recuperación socioeconómica justa y equitativa, con un enfoque anclado en el territorio a fin de reforzar la continuidad de apoyos urbano - rural. 

Este contexto plantea el desafío de trabajar en tres niveles de forma coordinada y amplia:
i) Macro: Apoyo al desarrollo de Políticas y Normas Nacionales para la recuperación socio-económica del sector productivo incluyendo sectores estratégicos y/o emergentes, que contribuyen a la reactivación socioeconómica integral. 
ii) Meso:  Desarrollo de Programas y Proyectos a nivel subnacional con enfoque de promoción de la industrialización con oportunidades de empleo, con enfoque intersectorial que aborden a poblaciones en situación de mayor vulnerabilidad. 
iii) Micro: Desarrollo de Acciones Piloto con productores/as y unidades económicas  a nivel urbano y rural, incluyendo asociaciones de pequeños/as agricultores/as, cooperativas y MIPYME.

Caribbean countries manage natural resources and ecosystems to strengthen their resilience and enhance the resilience and prosperity of the people and communities that depend on them.
planEntityVersion.description: Caribbean economies are highly dependent on the region’s natural resources and biodiverse ecosystems, both of which provide key services and co-benefits to people and communities. Economic resilience is, however, a critical challenge for the region in the face of environmental, climate and disaster risks, which collectively destroy natural resources and limit the region’s transformative capacity. The challenges of desertification, forest management, biodiversity loss and climate change are interrelated and need to be collectively addressed to achieve sustainable development in the Caribbean.  Both marine and terrestrial biodiversity conservation are acute issues requiring prioritization to ensure the sustainable use of ecosystems. Nature-based solutions that tackle overexploitation and address pollution and waste management should be optimised with specific attention provided to food and water security, a challenge that was further evidenced during the COVID-19 crisis.

Estado de derechos, instituciones  sólidas y cohesión social
planEntityVersion.description:
La Agenda 2030 para el Desarrollo Sostenible señala la necesidad de contar con instituciones eficaces, eficientes y transparentes, elementos indispensables para garantizar los derechos de las personas y para alcanzar los cambios esperados en otros ámbitos. El crimen organizado, las drogas ilícitas, las armas y actividades ilícitas como los delitos económicos y la corrupción han creado obstáculos severos para la construcción de la paz y la reforma del sector de la seguridad. Por ello, la Agenda 2030 y principalmente el ODS 16 apuntan a construir instituciones sólidas y transparentes, bajo un enfoque que vincula el desarrollo, la seguridad y los derechos humanos.

La Agenda Común, promovida por el Secretario General para acelerar la implementación de los ODS, refleja la necesidad de renovar el contrato social entre los Gobiernos y la población. Plantea la urgencia de restaurar la confianza dentro de cada sociedad, abrazar una concepción amplia de los derechos humanos, y promover la eliminación de la violencia basada en género en todos los ámbitos, así como la participación activa e igualitaria de las mujeres y las niñas, sin las cuales es imposible lograr un verdadero contrato social.

Por su parte, el eje institucional del Plan de Creación de Oportunidades 2021-2025 menciona la necesidad de recuperar la confianza ciudadana en las instituciones y el estado de derecho, para vivir una democracia plena. Incluye políticas relacionadas con independencia judicial, seguridad jurídica, conectividad, gobierno digital, migración, integridad pública y lucha contra la corrupción, entre otras. El eje de seguridad integral incluye políticas para enfrentar la delincuencia y el crimen organizado, y para mejorar el sistema de rehabilitación social, la seguridad vial y la seguridad del Estado.

planEntityVersion.name: En 2026, el Estado mejora la gestión pública e incrementa la protección y garantía de  derechos, la igualdad de género y la cohesión social, mientras reduce las amenazas  a la seguridad humana y promueve la erradicación de todas las formas de violencia.

Igualdad socioeconómica y transformación productiva sostenible
planEntityVersion.description:
La Agenda 2030 subraya la necesidad de una sociedad más igualitaria y de reducir las brechas socioeconómicas existentes. Busca aumentar la productividad, tanto 
en el sector industrial como en el sector agrícola, tomando en cuenta los impactos al medioambiente y a las futuras generaciones. También, aumentar el número de 
puestos de trabajo decentes, para asegurar que todas las personas puedan estar dentro del mercado formal de trabajo, así como una distribución más equitativa de 
ingresos y riqueza.

En la misma línea, la Agenda Común, lanzada por el Secretario General, llama a todos los países a facilitar la inclusión económica de las mujeres, a dar más importancia a los y las jóvenes para asegurar su inclusión en el mercado laboral, a reformar los sistemas tributarios, a asegurar una financiación sostenible y a tener en cuenta el medioambiente en el modelo económico. Todo esto es necesario no solo para alcanzar los objetivos de la Agenda 2030, sino para lograr una mayor igualdad 
socioeconómica y una transformación productiva sostenible.

El Plan de Creación de Oportunidades 2021-2025 reconoce la importancia de una transformación productiva e industrial sostenible, para tener una economía 
emprendedora, con oportunidades para todas las personas. Este plan también busca reducir la pobreza multidimensional y erradicar la pobreza extrema por ingresos, 
a través de la estabilidad macroeconómica y del fortalecimiento de un esquema productivo sostenible e innovador, que promueva oportunidades laborales. También se pretende reducir las brechas laborales en los ámbitos urbano y rural, y las brechas por sexo en el mercado laboral. El plan reconoce que “la discriminación sigue presente incluso en los empleos de alta calidad, en los que logran ingresar mujeres con buenos niveles de educación, pues las posibilidades de ascenso son menores (…)”.
